It's time for /v/Zelda's weekly Zelda Unknown discussion! We're going through the episodes week by week and having discussion threads here every friday. This week's episode, Deserts and the Missing Link, focuses around the Gerudo Desert, possible connections between the versions of it in Ocarina of Time and Twilight Princess, and the role it will play in Zelda U.

Please watch the episode and then join in the discussion: Zelda Unknown Episode 2: Deserts and the Missing Link

Episode Summary

Episode 2 focuses on the desert regions of Hyrule, the links between them, and what the region will be like in Zelda U. The Gerudo Desert appear's to be in the West of the Zelda U World Map, which Conrad circled here:

https://veuwer.com/i/2xbg.png

Cross-game connections between Gerudo Desert

The first theory of the video is that the deserts of Zelda U, Ocarina of Time, Twilight Princess, and Skyward Sword are all actually the same desert, with its geography being changed by time.

Connections

  • 3:00 - 3:52 Ancient Harbor (SS), Gerudo's Valley, and Gap (TP) are all the same location. These areas all have a similar shape, appearance and bridges.

  • 3:53 - 6:17 The Sandship in Skyward Sword and OoT's Gerudo Fortress have a similar shape and size. The Sandship was found by the Gerudo and made into their fortress after being lost and abandoned some time following Skyward Sword. In Twilight Princess, the structure is gone, probably having been destroyed around the time the Gerudo disappeared.

  • 6:17 - 8:44 Skipper's Retreat (SS), Phantom House/Haunted Wasteland (OoT), and Cave of Ordeals (TP). There is a very strong resemblence between the Skipper's House in SS and the Phantom House in OoT's Haunted Wasteland and they are likely the same building.

  • 8:45 - 12:04 Pirate Bay (SS, Desert Colossus (OoT), Bulbin Fortress (TP). All of these share a similar layout and are the last area explored before reaching a dungeon. Several other theories have concluded that the Spirit Temple in OoT and Twilight Princess's Arbiter's Grounds are the same area as well. Conrad expands these theories to include The Pirate Stronghold in SS. Once again, he theorizes that the Gerudo's ancestors found the Pirate Stronghold and converted it into the Spirit Temple, the ruins of which are the Arbiter's Grounds.

Zelda U Desert Region Speculations

12:05

The second half of the video focuses on what should be included in Zelda U's Desert. Conrad divides it into six sections:

Timeline Placement

12:39 - 13:55

The desert region has varied significantly over the timeline of the series, ranging from completely dead and isolated to full of life and enemies. This is likely due to the events of Ocarina of Time, the aftermath of which likely removed the Gerudo Race from Hyrule. Thus, if Zelda U takes place before Ocarina of Time, it will probably be one of the living deserts, and vice versa.

Races

13:56 - 15:17

Likewise, if Zelda U takes place before OoT, it could bring back the Gerudo, a race that has been absent for a long time in the series. It could also bring back the Ancient Robots from Skyward Sword, which disappeared somewhere between that game and OoT.

Geography

15:18 - 16:46

Like races, the geography of the desert in Zelda U also depends heavily on the game's timeline placement. However, it is certain to be a very vast region based again off Aonuma's statement that one region in Zelda U could be as big as the entire overworld of Twilight Princess. If the desert is of the dead variety that comes after OoT, this would bring many of the same problems Twilight Princess had with giant areas with very little content in them.

Urban Environments

16:47 - 17:45

The desert areas of the Zelda series so far have never featured a fully developed town. Conrad hopes that Zelda U will break this trend, introducing a true town possibly with Middle Eastern influences, a bazaar, and unique weaponry and items that cannot be purchased in other areas. The Gerudos should populate this town, and we should learn more about their culture and civilization before the events of OoT.

Wildlife/Enemies

17:46 - 18:37

The desert region in Zelda U should have a much larger variety of enemies than its previous incarnations, bringing back enemies like Snakes (LoZ) and Scorpians (SS). There should also be desert wildlife such as vultures, hyenas, spiders, camels, coyotes, tortoises, etc. Conrad wants Zelda U to introduce a new hunting mechanic where you can capture these animals and bring them to the bazaar in the Gerudo town to sell.

Dungeons

18:37 - 20:45

The dungeons in the Zelda series so far have been some of the best and most memorable in the series, like the Spirit Temple in OoT and Arbiter's Grounds in TP. Hopefully the dungeon in Zelda U's dungeon follows this trend. Conrad also hates eyes, and the dungeon boss in Zelda U better not have a fucking eye as a weakness.

Conclusion

20:45 - END

Topics for Discussion

Now that we've watched the video, please post any thoughts you have on it! I've created a few topics for discussion that I found particularly interesting, but feel free to post your own and reply to any, all or none of these in any order you like.

  1. What do you think of Conrad's theory that the deserts from OoT, SS, and TP are all actually the same desert? Is the evidence he gives enough to convince you?

  2. If the desert is in fact the same area with its geography changed by time, this would imply that the same is true in other areas in Hyrule. Is there any other area you see this in?

  3. As discussed, whether Zelda U takes place before or after OoT is extremely important to its contents and life. Are you hoping we have another barren, eerie desert like TP's, or one full of life, enemies and Gerudos?

  4. Where on the timeline do you want this desert to be? What particular events in the Desert's history would you like Zelda U to address?

  5. Do you want the Gerudo to return in Zelda U? Are there any other past races or species you would like to return in the game, or perhaps some new ones?
